section: Social Studies (Paper-2) · Ch46 — Ancient & Medieval India — Deep 3
subject: Social Studies
stem: The medieval devotional (Bhakti) movement, which emphasised a personal, direct relationship with God without ritual intermediaries and used regional languages instead of Sanskrit, was significant because it:

options.option_text: Promoted social equality and challenged rigid caste hierarchies through popular devotional practice
Strengthened the caste system and Sanskrit-only worship
Was confined only to South India with no wider impact
Rejected all forms of devotion to God

explanation: The Bhakti movement (with saints like Kabir, Meera, Ramanuja, Annamacharya) promoted direct, personal devotion in local languages, cutting across caste lines and challenging ritual/Brahmanical exclusivity.
